summary.intent: Use the GSD manager workflow to drive CipherBox milestone v2.0 to completion: verify/discuss/plan/execute several closeout phases (69, 70.1, 74, 75, 77), ship completed phases through the full ship-phase pipeline (verify/secure/validate/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR), and specifically root-cause and fix a persistent macOS-only Desktop-E2E rotation test failure on Phase 74's PR before merging.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 74, 75, and 77 were verified/executed and shipped; PR #607 (Phase 74) was merged to main after a deep multi-day investigation uncovered and fixed a real macOS FUSE-T rotation race condition (stale metadata refresh clobbering rotated keys) plus a token-TTL bug, both confirmed green in CI; PR #608 (Phase 75) was opened and, during ship, additional real cross-language crypto parity bugs (CBOR duplicate-key handling, UUID regex trailing-newline bug, RFC3339 fixed-width parsing) were found and fixed via CodeRabbit/Greptile review; phases 76, 78, 79 remain unplanned per user pause.

repo: GSD's plan-file scanner has a loose `/PLAN/i` substring fallback (plan-scan.cjs:28) that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' as a plan file, causing false 'Executing' dashboard status — fixed for one instance by renaming a file, but the scanner bug itself remains unpatched.

GSD's `phase uat-passed --require-verification` predicate needs a UAT.md to consider implementation complete even when verification already passed via CI/cargo (no human UAT applicable) — write a minimal UAT stub to unblock.

Two incompatible wire-encoding domains coexist with no type-level enforcement: internal node-codec/stored sealed refs use base64, but all share-API DTOs (create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) validate encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey/itemNameEncrypted as HEX — this exact class of bug has recurred multiple times.

macOS uses FUSE-T with an SMB backend (not a real kernel FUSE); Linux uses fuser/libfuse3; Windows uses WinFsp — behavioral differences between these (e.g. whether `open()` is called on rename source/dest) cause macOS-only failures that Linux/Windows tests never surface.

Building the desktop binary links macFUSE by default unless PKG_CONFIG_PATH is overridden with a FUSE-T-aliased fuse.pc — CI explicitly copies fuse-t.pc to override this; local dev must replicate it non-destructively.

API access-token TTL is hardcoded 15m; the desktop client authenticates once at startup with no auto-refresh-on-401 (test-login path skips Keychain refresh-token storage), so long-running headless test sessions can token-expire mid-run.
sdk-e2e vitest tests do not load .env — SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported inline or the harness falls back to a default secret that the API rejects with 401.

code.finding: Fix: after a scope-exit rotation refreshes inode keys, mark the rotated folders as `mutated_folders` so the existing `drain_refresh_completions` guard prevents a stale in-flight metadata refresh from clobbering the freshly-rotated keys via `apply_owned_children`.

`drain_refresh_completions` already guards `mutated_folders`/`publish_queue` folders by calling `mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved` (preserves keys) instead of `apply_owned_children` (clobbers keys) — this pre-existing guard is what the rotation fix leverages.
`apply_owned_children`'s File arm re-materializes children with `cid: String::new()` and a freshly-derived read_key, resetting any previously-refreshed key — this is the clobbering mechanism.

SC#2 grant re-mint bug: `base64_encode`'d the wrapped `encryptedReadKey` for share-grant update, but the API's update-grant DTO validates it as hex — fixed to hex-encode; internal node-codec fields correctly remain base64.

Rotation republish sets `write_sealed: None` on republished nodes (write-plane preservation deliberately deferred) — causes owned-walks to fail and prevents replay-based signing-seed recovery; real durability bug, captured as a todo rather than fixed in-branch.
Access token TTL hardcoded to `15m`; made configurable via `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` env var (production default unchanged) to unblock long-running headless E2E test sessions.

`CANONICAL_UUID_RE` used JS `$` without the `m` flag, which also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a UUID+`\n` string was incorrectly accepted — real SC3 soundness/parity gap vs. the Rust side which checks exact byte length.

IPNS CBOR decoders only rejected duplicate keys for their 4 security-relevant fields, silently ignoring duplicates of other fields (e.g. TTL) — tightened to reject any duplicate map key for full TS/Rust parity (Greptile P1 finding).

Plan-file matcher has a loose fallback: any `.md` file whose name merely contains the substring 'PLAN' (case-insensitive) is counted as a plan file, causing miscounts (e.g. `*-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md` miscounted as a 26th plan).

workflow: Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot `EnterWorktree` into a pre-existing worktree — the working pattern for resuming interrupted background planning/execution is sequential processing on the main checkout switched per feat branch, not worktree re-entry.

When a background agent's result claims 'cargo/tests green' but the harness surfaces an unrelated compiler diagnostic (e.g. rust-analyzer E0277 anchored at a stdlib location with no matching file in the repo), verify with an actual `cargo check`/`cargo test` run rather than trusting the agent summary.

Never characterize a CI failure as an 'infra flake' without reading the actual failure log end-to-end — an early hasty '401 infra flake' conclusion here was wrong and the real cause required an 8+ hour local-reproduction investigation to find (a genuine rotation-engine correctness bug).

When a test passes on some platforms and fails consistently on one, treat platform-specific op semantics (e.g. does `rename()` call `open()` on the destination/source) as the prime suspect before assuming flakiness.

Empirically confirm hypotheses with instrumented reproduction runs before touching a crypto/resolve seam — an early hypothesis (API IPNS resolve lag) was refuted by one instrumented run, avoiding a wrong fix to production resolve logic.

GSD's todo auto-close on `phase.complete` can under-close: todos correctly tagged `resolves_phase: N` can be left stranded in pending/ even though the shipped code resolved them — worth auditing pending todos against merged diffs before starting a new phase's ship flow.

friction: Early mischaracterization of the macOS Desktop-E2E failure as a '401 infra flake' was wrong — user had to correct this twice (first for the general framing, then with a pasted log showing the real EACCES/write_sealed error), triggering a full multi-hour local-reproduction investigation.

Sub-agents cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree when launched from the repo root — this failure mode recurred across the autonomous resume sessions and required pivoting the whole orchestration strategy to sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch.

Repeated session/quota limit interruptions during the autonomous overnight run required multiple CronCreate-based resumes, several of which had to be corrected mid-flight because the resume instructions encoded a since-abandoned (worktree) strategy.
macFUSE vs FUSE-T library linking gotcha caused an initial local build to silently link the wrong FUSE backend, invalidating an early reproduction attempt.
Stale FUSE-T mount / leftover go-nfsv4 process required manual force-unmount and process kill before a clean remount.

Root-causing the macOS rotation bug took ~10 full local reproduction cycles (~10 min each) across multiple wrong hypotheses (write_sealed preservation, read-path self-heal, coalesced dest-gate exclusion, API resolve lag) before the actual mutated_folders fix was found.
gsd commit helper occasionally false-negatives `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands, requiring manual `git log` verification instead of blind retries.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility; PR body updates must go through `gh api -X PATCH`.
A CI Typecheck failure (mock fixtures not updated for a widened return type) slipped past local vitest (which doesn't type-check) and was only caught by the CI `tsc --noEmit` gate.
Desktop-E2E's dispatch-gated workflow_dispatch trigger required manual re-dispatching multiple times as fixes landed, extending the overall ship cycle.
